exposure: Maternal perceived stress during late pregnancy (10-item Perceived Stress Scale score)
outcome: Infant adiposity (fat mass, lean mass, FM-related ratios, weight)
cohort: Mother-infant dyads (N = 138) from the ongoing MADRES cohort, predominantly a low-income Hispanic population.
finding: A 1-SD higher maternal perceived stress score during late pregnancy was associated with higher infant fat mass percentage at 1 month, with stronger associations observed among male and preterm infants.
